question: Should OpenClaw permanently support `skills-sh:owner/repo/slug` as a core CLI contract for ClawHub-resolved, explicitly unscanned external skill entries?
rationale: The implementation can be mechanically reviewed, but accepting a new long-lived user-facing reference grammar and managed unscanned-code path is a product and security-boundary choice that cannot be inferred from contributor-authored proof alone.

options.title: Confirm and land the colon contract
options.body: Adopt the explicit colon grammar, retaining commit-pinned ClawHub resolution and visible unscanned provenance as mandatory invariants.

options.title: Keep external entries outside core
options.body: Decline the new CLI grammar and direct users to existing ClawHub publishing or unmanaged `git:` installation paths instead.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Specify a different supported external-reference boundary before accepting an implementation.

recommendation.title: Confirm and land the colon contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the explicit colon grammar, retaining commit-pinned ClawHub resolution and visible unscanned provenance as mandatory invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context identifies this contributor as the contact who documented the proposed contract and demonstrated its lifecycle behavior; a current-main owner could not be resolved in the available inspection environment.
